speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of the breast mass you are presenting with, could you please describe when you first noticed it and if you have experienced any pain or nipple discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the mass feel hard or fixed to the surrounding tissue, and have you noticed any skin changes like dimpling or redness? Are you currently experiencing any pain in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid growth over just four weeks, I need to rule out aggressive malignancies or inflammatory conditions. Do you have any history of breast cancer, and is there a family history of breast or ovarian cancer in your close relatives? REQUEST TEST: Mammography

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mammogram shows a smooth polylobulated mass, which is reassuring, but the rapid growth over four weeks is concerning and requires further characterization. REQUEST TEST: Breast Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The discrepancy between the palpable rapid growth and the benign-appearing imaging is unusual, so I need to rule out a phyllodes tumor or a rapidly growing fibroadenoma. Have you ever been pregnant or are you currently taking any hormonal therapies? REQUEST TEST: Core Needle Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Image shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth is diagnostic for a phyllodes tumor. DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes Tumor
